methods.notes: Source-derived substring match used by the official API scanner. No service-only matcher is declared: the API service's advertisement presence is unverified and the standard BLE-MIDI service is shared by unrelated instruments. User confirmation is required when the name is ambiguous.

identification.notes: The official API scanner selects advertisements whose local name contains the case-sensitive substring Wave. That is a reported heuristic, not a unique product identifier. Confirm the expected service after connection and let the user resolve similarly named peripherals. The vendor API and standard MIDI service UUIDs are not asserted to appear in advertisements.

device.name: Wave by Genki
device.notes: A gesture-control ring with two separate local Bluetooth modes. Standalone mode is standard BLE-MIDI. The vendor API mode instead uses Genki's GATT service, COBS frames and motion/spectrogram payloads. Do not send API-mode writes on the MIDI characteristic, and do not treat the API characteristic as though it carried BLE-MIDI. Neither path needs a cloud account.

openness.notes: Genki publishes the API and adapters for third-party use. This document restates their wire format; it does not claim compatibility with any firmware other than the source's compatibility target, and it does not identify a latest firmware release.

enter_pairing_mode.notes: The official API connects directly and documents no PIN, but it also discusses an OS-paired Linux host. That is insufficient to make a universal claim about bonding requirements on every host or firmware.

exclusivity.recovery: Close the other MIDI/API client. On Linux, the official README notes that the OS may auto-connect after pairing; disconnect that OS connection before opening the direct API client.

pairing.notes: No universal pairing or single-central claim is made. The API's direct connection sequence and the standalone host MIDI flow are reported facts; link-layer bonding remains to be checked on hardware.

credentials.notes: No Wi-Fi passphrase, API key or account credential is used by either documented local route. Persistent OS-level bond state is not asserted.

factory_reset.description: The pinned official API documentation gives power on/off instructions but no factory-reset procedure. Do not substitute power cycling or an API configuration write for a reset.
factory_reset.effect: No factory-reset effect or procedure is established. Holding the top and bottom buttons for one second is documented as power-off, not as a factory reset.

methods.basis: Official API README and standalone MIDI example at the pinned commit; not replayed against hardware.
methods.description: Use the host's normal MIDI stack. This route does not use Genki's API characteristic, API-mode request or COBS framing.
methods.name: Standalone standard BLE-MIDI

steps.action: Press the middle button to turn on Wave and close other clients connected to it.
Select the intended Wave peripheral in the host MIDI interface; do not identify it by the generic MIDI service alone.
Connect to the standard BLE-MIDI service and enable notifications on 7772e5db-3868-4112-a1a9-f2669d106bf3.
Decode standard BLE-MIDI messages; make no Genki API writes in this mode.

methods.basis: Official Python, Android and C++ API implementations at the pinned commit; not replayed against hardware.
methods.description: Connect directly to Genki's API service, subscribe, enter API mode, then send either an 8-byte configuration or the distinct extended 12-byte configuration. Use the complete COBS writes declared below.
methods.name: Genki motion-data API

steps.action: Press the middle button to turn on Wave. Disconnect the OS or any other client that already holds the ring.
Connect to the peripheral the user confirmed and locate the Genki API service 65e9296c-8dfb-11ea-bc55-0242ac130003.
Write the enter_api_mode command, then write one API configuration command; do not send both 8-byte and 12-byte configurations.
Buffer notifications across arbitrary BLE boundaries, split complete COBS frames at zero bytes, and validate the four-byte header before decoding a payload.
On shutdown, stop notifications and disconnect cleanly rather than killing the session.

setup.notes: Both routes are local and account-free. Choose standalone BLE-MIDI for ordinary MIDI performance, or the API route for structured motion data. The API route must enter API mode before selecting exactly one suitable configuration. The two configuration widths are not interchangeable.

rejoin.notes: There is no Wi-Fi membership to migrate. Close the previous central, then reconnect and repeat the selected mode's connection sequence.

testing.notes: No device was connected or driven by this project. Protocol facts are reported from the official API repository at 08addce0ea5377bfa48bbb8debae20f19c4df725 and the genki-wave 0.5.3 source release. All byte strings in fixed_write_vectors are synthetic constructions from those layouts, independently checked by scripts/test_genki_wave.py; they are not owner traffic.

artifacts.artifact: Wave product page and official API README
artifacts.description: Product identity and local music-control purpose. The README supplies standalone mode and connection caveats.

evidence.documentation_review: The official README distinguishes standalone BLE-MIDI from direct API use, documents power on/off and describes clean-disconnect and Linux auto-connect issues. No factory reset or universal host bonding rule was found.
evidence.official_source_review: Reviewed the official Python, Android and C++ adapters and examples at 08addce0ea5377bfa48bbb8debae20f19c4df725 (2025-04-10). The Python header format is <BBH, establishing type u8, id u8 and payload_size u16le. The original Python configuration is eight bytes; the C++ structure adds a final float and is twelve bytes with the same two reserved bytes. The source's reassembly and layout facts are reported, not hardware-confirmed.
evidence.open_questions: No owner GATT dump or short motion/device-info capture has been checked. Sensor/spectrogram units and calibration, bin frequencies, timestamp epoch, battery wire padding, address display order, exact GATT permissions, standalone mapping on the target firmware, factory reset and host bonding behavior remain open.

ApiConfig12.description: Extended twelve-byte configuration payload for package id 11, represented by the official C++ API. The final float exists only in this form.

fields.description: Two zero padding bytes before the first float.
fields.name: reserved

fields.description: Official example UI ranges from 0.0 to 1.0; physical calibration is not established.
fields.name: tap_sensitivity

parse_rules: Require exactly twelve payload bytes and header payload_size 12.
Keep this extended layout distinct from ApiConfig8 in encoders, logs and tests.

ApiConfig8.description: Original eight-byte configuration payload for package id 11. It ends after sample_rate and carries no tap-sensitivity float.

fields.description: Two zero padding bytes in the official packed layout.
fields.name: reserved

parse_rules: Require exactly eight payload bytes and header payload_size 8.
Do not read tap_sensitivity from this form and do not silently widen it to ApiConfig12.

ApiHeader.description: Four-byte header before COBS encoding. The package id is ONE unsigned byte. Only payload_size is a 16-bit little-endian value; it counts payload bytes only, excluding this header, COBS expansion and the zero delimiter.

fields.description: Package id u8, not u16le; see protocol_details.api_framing.package_ids.
fields.name: id

fields.description: Exact number of bytes following the four-byte header.
fields.name: payload_size

parse_rules: COBS-decode one complete nonzero-delimited frame before reading this header.
Require at least four decoded bytes, then require len(frame) == 4 + payload_size.
Reject an unknown id or a payload size/layout mismatch rather than decoding a plausible prefix.

BatteryStatus.description: Nine meaningful battery field bytes (package id 2). The Android decoder reads these fields without checking the total length. The official C++ value type is naturally aligned and commonly occupies twelve bytes, adding three trailing ABI padding bytes; actual on-wire length and trailing-byte values have not been captured.
parse_rules: Require at least the nine field bytes and honor the header payload_size; is_charging is zero for false and nonzero for true in the official Android decoder.

Accept the nine-byte field-only form. Also tolerate a twelve-byte native-layout candidate by preserving, not decoding, its three trailing bytes. Do not claim either wire width is confirmed without a capture.

DeviceInfo.description: A 35-byte device-information response (package id 3). This describes the layout only; no owner address or serial is included in this spec.

fields.description: UTF-8 text with trailing NUL bytes trimmed; fixed nine-byte field.
fields.name: board_version

fields.description: Per-unit address bytes; display order differs between official adapters and must not be used as an identity matcher.
fields.name: bluetooth_address

fields.description: Per-unit UTF-8 text with trailing NUL bytes trimmed; fixed seventeen-byte field.
fields.name: serial_number

parse_rules: Require exactly 35 bytes and render firmware as major.minor.patch.
Treat address and serial as private per-unit values. Do not publish them in captures or use them as product-wide facts.
The Python adapter displays address bytes in forward order while the C++ example reverses them; canonical display order remains unresolved.

MotionData.description: A 105-byte motion payload (package id 1). Every float is IEEE-754 binary32 little-endian and every offset is packed; there is no alignment padding before peak_norm_velocity or timestamp_us. Quaternion component order is w, x, y, z. Euler component order is roll, pitch, yaw.
parse_rules: Require exactly 105 bytes; offsets 92, 93 and 97 are intentionally unaligned.

Physical units and calibration for gyro, acceleration, magnetometer, Euler angles, linear acceleration and peak_norm_velocity are not established by the cited parser; leave them raw and do not infer degrees, radians, g, m/s² or µT.
Quaternion values are dimensionless. timestamp_us is the device stream's microsecond counter; its epoch and wrap behavior are not established.
The API derives gravity as acc minus linear_acc and can rotate acc/linear_acc by current_pose; those are client-side derived values, not extra wire fields.

RawMotionData.description: A 32-byte raw accelerometer/gyro payload (package id 9), with the same unresolved sensor units as MotionData.
parse_rules: Require exactly 32 bytes. Do not infer physical sensor units from the float representation.

SpectrogramData.description: A 392-byte spectrogram column (package id 10): 96 little-endian float32 values followed by a microsecond counter. Each channel has 16 consecutive bins. Bin frequencies, FFT/window parameters, magnitude/power units and calibration are unknown; the floats are not labeled Hz, dB or physical sensor units.

fields.description: Sixteen consecutive float32 values, bin 0 through bin 15.
fields.name: acc_x_bins

parse_rules: Require exactly 392 bytes: 96 * 4 data bytes plus 8 timestamp bytes.
Channel index c selects floats [16*c .. 16*c+15] in the order acc x/y/z then gyro x/y/z.
Do not assign bin-center frequencies, dB scaling or physical units without new evidence.

cobs_rules: Construct type:u8 | id:u8 | payload_size:u16le | payload, then COBS-encode the entire sequence and append one 00 delimiter.
COBS body bytes never include 00. The delimiter is not passed to the COBS decoder and is not counted by payload_size.
The id is one byte at decoded offset 1; do not pack it as u16le and do not move payload_size.
command_order: Send enter_api_mode exactly once for the API session.
Choose one configuration. The two fixed 8-byte examples and the extended 12-byte example document alternatives, not a sequence to send together.
Issue battery/device-info requests only in API mode, and cleanly stop notifications and disconnect at session end.

package_ids.6: identify (not implemented as a command here)
package_ids.7: recenter (not implemented as a command here)
package_ids.8: display frame (not implemented as a command here)

receive_reassembly: Maintain a byte buffer across notifications. Append each notification in order; BLE may fragment one COBS frame or coalesce several frames and a trailing partial frame.
At each 00 byte, remove and COBS-decode the preceding nonempty body. Empty bodies between adjacent delimiters carry no package.
Retain a final nonempty fragment without a delimiter for the next notification. Never decode a partial fragment early.
After COBS decode, validate the four-byte header and exact payload_size before selecting a payload layout. Drop an invalid encoded frame and resume at the next delimiter.
Reset the reassembly buffer on disconnect. No extra fragment header or BLE-MIDI timestamp is present on the API characteristic.

firmware_scope.notes: The pinned API source contains a compatibility constant 1.7.4. It is not evidence that this is the latest firmware, not a minimum/maximum claim for every unit, and not a firmware-update procedure. No update was attempted and no DFU mechanism is asserted by this spec.

fixed_write_vectors.description: Constructed solely from the official layouts. raw_hex is the complete pre-COBS header and payload; write_hex is the exact synthetic GATT write. These vectors contain no owner identifiers and are not captured traffic.

standalone_ble_midi.notes: Standalone mode uses the standard BLE-MIDI packet format and ordinary MIDI tooling. It shares no COBS framing or package ids with API mode. Genki's example maps B0 CC 16/17/18 to pitch/yaw/roll; no claim is made that these assignments cannot be changed by standalone configuration software.

remaining_unknowns: Physical units/calibration for gyro, acceleration, magnetometer, Euler angles, linear acceleration and peak_norm_velocity are not established; retain raw float32 values.
Battery has nine meaningful field bytes, but the actual wire payload_size and any three-byte native trailing padding need a capture.
Spectrogram bin-center frequencies, FFT/window details and magnitude/power units are unknown.
Timestamp epoch/wrap behavior and canonical DeviceInfo address display order need hardware evidence.
No factory-reset procedure or universal OS pairing/bonding behavior is established.
The exact advertised name across modes/firmware and whether each service UUID is advertised need an owner scan/GATT dump.
No latest-firmware claim or firmware-update path is established; 1.7.4 is only the pinned source compatibility constant.
Button payload timestamp semantics and commands outside the minimal documented set are intentionally not exposed here.

configure_motion_8_byte.description: Select the original 8-byte API configuration: motion stream 1, spectrogram disabled, sample rate 400.0 Hz. This payload has no tap-sensitivity field; it is not the extended configuration.

configure_motion_extended_12_byte.description: Synthetic extended 12-byte configuration based on the official C++ layout: motion stream 1, spectrogram disabled, 400.0 Hz, tap sensitivity 0.7. This is a separate payload width, not the original 8-byte command with four implicit bytes appended.

configure_spectrogram_8_byte.description: Select the original 8-byte API configuration: datastream 0, spectrogram enabled, sample rate 2000.0 Hz. No tap-sensitivity field is present.

enter_api_mode.description: Request device mode 103 (API). Send after subscribing and before any API configuration. Unframed payload is type 1, id 5, payload_size 1, payload 67.

request_battery_status.description: Request a BatteryStatus payload (type 1, id 2, zero payload bytes), after entering API mode.

request_device_info.description: Request a DeviceInfo payload (type 1, id 3, zero payload bytes), after entering API mode.

characteristics.name: Genki API request and stream
characteristics.notes: Every command value below is a complete GATT write: COBS body plus its trailing 00 delimiter. Do not COBS-encode it a second time and do not add a BLE-MIDI header. Incoming notifications are an arbitrary byte stream, not one-frame-per-notification messages. The official clients use both write-with-response and write-without-response adapters; actual per-unit GATT permissions have not been dumped.

initialization.notes: Subscribe before writing enter_api_mode and a configuration. This initialization step is scoped to the API service; never run it as a reason to send API writes to the MIDI service.

services.name: Genki Wave API service
services.notes: Vendor API mode only. COBS/zero-delimited packets share one characteristic for requests and notifications. The standard BLE-MIDI service below is a separate operating mode, not an alias for this service.

characteristics.name: Standard BLE-MIDI I/O
characteristics.notes: Standard BLE-MIDI packets only. The official example receives MIDI CC status B0 and maps controller 16 to pitch, 17 to yaw and 18 to roll. Those assignments describe the example's standalone mapping, not the Genki API motion payload and not a universal user remapping.

initialization.notes: Standard BLE-MIDI input; use a normal BLE-MIDI packet parser.

services.name: Standard BLE-MIDI service (standalone mode)
services.notes: Standard MIDI path documented by Genki's standalone example. It is not unique to Wave and is deliberately absent from automatic identification. No Genki API command is valid on this service.
